title: PHY 101 ( UNINIGER ) : MOTION IN ONE DIMENSION
subject: Phy

questions.question: Particle kinematics studies motion without considering which factor?
questions.explanation: Particle kinematics studies motion without considering the causes of motion.

questions.question: Any change in position during a time interval is called which term?
questions.explanation: Motion is defined as any change in the position of a particle during a time interval.

questions.question: Which path type produces curvilinear translational motion?
questions.explanation: Curvilinear translational motion occurs when the path is curved.

questions.question: Motion of a car from Awka to Onitsha is an example of which motion?
questions.explanation: The car changes position from one place to another along a path.

questions.question: Rectilinear translational motion follows which path?
questions.explanation: Rectilinear translational motion occurs along a straight line.

questions.question: Motion of a simple pendulum bob about its equilibrium position is an example of which motion?
questions.explanation: A pendulum bob moves to and fro about a fixed equilibrium point.

questions.question: Dust and smoke particles exhibit which motion?
questions.explanation: Dust and smoke particles move in an irregular and haphazard manner.

questions.question: Random motion has no defined path or which other feature?
questions.explanation: Random motion has no defined path and no defined direction.

questions.question: Motion of fan blades is an example of which motion?
questions.explanation: Fan blades move about a fixed position, which is rotational motion.

questions.question: Location of a body at a particular instant is called which term?
questions.explanation: Position is the location of a body at a particular instant of time.

questions.question: Total path travelled by a body is called which quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance is the total path travelled by a body.

questions.question: Distance is classified as which type of quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance has magnitude only and is therefore a scalar quantity.

questions.question: Displacement is classified as which type of quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction and is a vector quantity.

questions.question: Displacement equation uses final position minus which position?
questions.explanation: Displacement equals final position minus initial position.

questions.question: Total distance covered per unit time defines which quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is the total distance covered by a particle per unit time.

questions.question: Average speed equals distance divided by which quantity?
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by the time interval.

questions.question: Instantaneous speed is the limiting value of average speed as time interval approaches which value?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous speed is obtained as the time interval approaches zero.

questions.question: S.I. unit of speed is which unit?
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of speed is metre per second.

questions.question: Speed is scalar because it lacks which feature?
questions.explanation: Speed has no direction and is therefore a scalar quantity.

questions.question: Average velocity is displacement divided by which quantity?
questions.explanation: Average velocity is displacement divided by the time interval.

questions.question: Instantaneous velocity is the limiting value of average velocity as time interval approaches which value?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is obtained as the time interval approaches zero.

questions.question: Instantaneous velocity equals which derivative?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time.

questions.question: Velocity is classified as which type of quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction and is a vector quantity.

questions.question: S.I. unit of velocity is which unit?
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of velocity is metre per second.

questions.question: Average velocity is the rate of change of distance in a specified what?
questions.explanation: Average velocity is the rate of change of distance in a specified direction.

questions.question: Average acceleration is rate of change of which quantity?
questions.explanation: Average acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

questions.question: Instantaneous acceleration equals which derivative?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.

questions.question: S.I. unit of acceleration is which unit?
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of acceleration is metre per second square.

questions.question: Acceleration is defined as limiting value of average acceleration as time interval approaches which value?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous acceleration is obtained as the time interval approaches zero.

questions.question: Velocity as a function of time is integral of which quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is obtained by integrating acceleration with respect to time.

questions.question: Position as a function of time is integral of which quantity?
questions.explanation: Position is obtained by integrating velocity with respect to time.

questions.question: Integration formula for tⁿ has denominator given by which expression?
questions.explanation: The integral of tⁿ is t raised to n plus 1 divided by n plus 1.

questions.question: In Example 3.4 initial velocity is given as which value?
questions.explanation: Example 3.4 states that the initial velocity is 2 m/s.

questions.question: In Example 3.4 initial position is given as which value?
questions.explanation: Example 3.4 states that the initial position is 4 m.

questions.question: Displacement-time graph plots displacement against which variable?
questions.explanation: A displacement-time graph plots displacement on the y-axis and time on the x-axis.

questions.question: Slope of displacement-time graph gives which quantity?
questions.explanation: The slope of a displacement-time graph gives velocity.

questions.question: Velocity-time graph plots velocity against which variable?
questions.explanation: A velocity-time graph plots velocity on the y-axis and time on the x-axis.

questions.question: Area under velocity-time graph gives which quantity?
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph gives total displacement.

questions.question: Slope of velocity-time graph gives which quantity?
questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration.

questions.question: In Example 3.5 total distance is which value?
questions.explanation: The area under the graph in Example 3.5 gives 1200 m.

questions.question: Uniform motion has which acceleration?
questions.explanation: Uniform motion has constant velocity and therefore zero acceleration.

questions.question: Non-uniform motion has which velocity behavior?
questions.explanation: Non-uniform motion involves a changing velocity.

questions.question: Uniform acceleration means velocity changes at which rate?
questions.explanation: Uniform acceleration means velocity changes at a constant rate.

questions.question: In v = u + at, the symbol a represents which quantity?
questions.explanation: In the equation v = u + at, a represents acceleration.

questions.question: In v² = u² + 2as, the symbol s represents which quantity?
questions.explanation: In v² = u² + 2as, s represents displacement.

questions.question: In s = ut + ½at², the symbol s represents which quantity?
questions.explanation: In s = ut + ½at², s represents displacement.

questions.question: Equation s = average velocity times t applies to which acceleration?
questions.explanation: The equation uses average velocity and applies to uniform acceleration.

questions.question: Example 3.6 final velocity of the car is which value?
questions.explanation: Example 3.6 gives a final velocity of 12 m/s.

questions.question: Example 3.8 distance travelled in the sixth complete second is which value?
questions.explanation: Example 3.8 obtains 49.5 m for the sixth complete second.

questions.question: Newton developed the equations of motion for particles travelling with which acceleration?
questions.explanation: Newton's equations of motion apply to uniform acceleration on a straight line.
